scope: Focused independent source review of retained candidate process-trace accounting and nine newly authored evaluator controls. No whole-compiler or all-history review is claimed.
finding: The preceding evaluator allowed any number of allowed LLVM utility processes in a session. Candidate-reported counters alone could not prove absence of repeated artifact work in a no-op request.
reviewed_correction: Externally observed readiness and response boundaries capture trace bytes, sizes and hashes. Final reconciliation requires every captured prefix to remain unchanged.

Each response interval accounts for actual PID-specific successful chdir, exact executable and argv, and eventual child exit status. Missing, extra and failed artifact executions cannot be hidden by candidate reports.
No-op and non-emitting request records require an empty artifact command inventory. The actual trace interval must match it.
Split calls cannot cross a response boundary. New work after the final response is refused, while delayed exit and signal observations remain admissible.

The actual Rust caller records command Debug text, numeric process exit status, and label.stdout/stderr bytes. Command expectations match its exact llvm-ar and llvm-objcopy arguments, ordering, working directory and preserved streams.

The pinned Rust source confirms nonalternate Unix Command Debug uses the expected working-directory prefix and quoted program/arguments. This relies on the bounded fixture's ordinary ASCII paths and arguments, not arbitrary Debug syntax.
Initial trace capture is within startup cleanup. The shared original one-shot trace parser remains unchanged.

history_and_consumer_constants.meaning: Fixed authored expectations, not observed passes.

verdict: No source blocker found for exact-source hosted qualification.
remaining_scope: The trace bounds observed external artifact work. In-process parser/checker/TinyCC counters still require source correspondence and real execution; this change does not itself measure speed or qualify the public compiler.
